segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Good morning everyone, and welcome to the Museum of Farming Life.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I understand it’s your first visit here, so I’d like to give you some background information about the museum and then explain a little about what you can see during your visit.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So, where we’re standing at the moment is the entrance to a large building that was constructed in 1880 as the home of a local businessman.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Alfred Palmer, of the Palmer biscuit factory.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It was later sold and became a hall of residence for students in 1911, and a museum in 1951.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In 2005, a modern extension was built to accommodate the museum’s collections.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The museum’s owned by the university, and apart from two rooms that are our offices, the university uses the main part of the building.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You may see students going into the building for lessons, but it’s not open to museum visitors, I’m afraid.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It’s a shame because the interior architectural features are outstanding, especially the room that used to be the library.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Luckily, we’ve managed to keep entry to the museum free.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This includes access to all the galleries, outdoor areas and the rooms for special exhibitions.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We run activities for children and students, such as the museum club, for which there’s no charge.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We do have a donation box just over there so feel free to give whatever amount you consider appropriate.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We do have a cloakroom, if you’d like to leave your coats and bags somewhere.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Unlike other museums, photography is allowed here, so you might like to keep your cameras with you.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You might be more comfortable not carrying around heavy rucksacks, though keep your coats and jackets on as it’s quite cold in the museum garden today. —— I’d like to tell you about the different areas of the museum.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Just inside, and outside the main gallery, we have an area called Four Seasons.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Here you can watch a four-minute animation of a woodland scene.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It was designed especially for the museum by a group of young people on a film studies course, and it’s beautiful.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Children absolutely love it, but then, so do adults.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The main gallery’s called Town and Country.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It includes a photographic collection of prize-winning sheep and shepherds.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Leaving Town and Country, you enter Farmhouse Kitchen, which is ... well, self-explanatory.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Here we have the oldest collection of equipment for making butter and cheese in the country.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And this morning, a specialist cheesemaker will be giving demonstrations of how it’s produced.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You may even get to try some.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: After that, you can go in two directions.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: To the right is a staircase that takes you up to a landing from where you can look down on the galleries.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: To the left is a room called A Year on the Farm.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There’s lots of seating here as sometimes we use the room for school visits, so it’s a good place to stop for a rest.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: If you’re feeling competitive, you can take our memory test in which you answer questions about things you’ve seen in the museum.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The next area’s called Wagon Walk.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This contains farm carts from nearly every part of the country.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It’s surprising how much regional variation there was.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Beside the carts are display boards with information about each one.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The carts are old and fragile, so we ask you to keep your children close to you and ensure they don’t climb on the carts.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: From Wagon Walk, you can either make your way back to reception or go out into the garden – or even go back to take another look in the galleries.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In the far corner of the garden is Bees are Magic, but we’re redeveloping this area so you can’t visit that at the moment.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You can still buy our honey in the shop, though.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Finally, there’s The Pond, which contains all kinds of interesting wildlife.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There are baby ducks that are only a few days old, as well as tiny frogs.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The Pond isn’t deep and there’s a fence around it, so it’s perfectly safe for children.
